summary: All 16 units were reviewed in full, including relative-acceleration after its re-import. Every numeric key, worked example and tolerance was recomputed independently in Python (rigid-body kinematics, IC and slider-crank IC, relative acceleration, Coriolis, gear trains including epicyclic, cams, transmission angle, inertia, work-energy, impulse, centre of percussion, gyroscopic couple and precession, rolling and winch kinetics) and all agree with the keys. Direction conventions the author flagged (gyroscopic couple sign and ship-pitch yaw direction, vehicle load transfer in a left turn, forward/backward whirl, Aronhold-Kennedy and four-bar IC senses) were re-derived with vector cross products and are correct. No LaTeX control characters, literal unicode-escape text, '[object Object]' or garbled characters were found. Only minor clarity/consistency items remain. This is an AI review; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: Special case (b) says that for parallel but unequal velocities 'the IC lies on the common line through A and B'. This only holds when A and B lie on a common perpendicular to the velocities. (Rigid-body constraint forbids unequal parallel velocities otherwise.) The marking guide and q009 explanation ('the perpendiculars coincide') repeat the omission.
issues.suggestedFix: State the condition: A and B on the same line perpendicular to the two parallel velocities; the IC is where the line through the velocity-arrow tips meets that line.

issues.problem: Skidding wheel: centre moves forward at 6 m/s while the wheel 'spins at 30 rad/s', but the spin sense is not stated. The key (IC 0.20 m below the centre) assumes the spin is the forward-rolling sense; with the opposite sense the IC would be above the centre.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'in the sense of forward rolling' to the stem. Key c (0.20 m below the centre, 0.10 m above the ground) is correct under that assumption.

issues.problem: Common-errors callout: 'using I13 distances on the slider instead of on the rod'. The slider speed is v_B = omega_3 * BI13 (B is a point common to rod and slider pin), exactly as the lesson and worked example use, so this warning contradicts the method and is unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with a clearer warning, e.g. do not use omega_2 (crank rate) or the crank pin distance from O2 for the slider; use omega_3 and the distance from B to I13.

issues.problem: Common-errors text: 'Treating r-dot as the absolute radial speed when r changes while the arm turns (it is correct for the radial part but the transverse part must be added)' calls the same thing an error and correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword: omitting the transverse term r*omega when the arm turns, i.e. using only r-dot as the absolute speed.

issues.problem: The torque-ratio equation writes T_out/T_in = ... = T_driven/T_driver * eta where T on the right means tooth numbers, while T is torque on the left (and tooth number T_A etc. in the same lesson). The tabular-method description turns the sun '+1' revolution but the worked examples use +y. q007 explanation uses 'P' for planet teeth without defining it.
issues.suggestedFix: Use N or z for tooth numbers or write the tooth ratio explicitly; say 'turn the sun +y (e.g. +1) revolutions'; define the planet tooth count (T_P) in q007.

issues.problem: Slider-crank worked example first step is plain text ('x = sqrt(0.40^2 - 0.10^2)', 'omega_3', 'v_A') rather than LaTeX, and says 'so the vector from A to B is as shown' although no figure exists. Numbers are correct (omega_3=0, alpha_3=645.5 rad/s^2 ccw, a_B=64.5 m/s^2 in +x all re-derived).
issues.suggestedFix: Typeset the step in LaTeX and drop 'as shown' (or state r_B/A = (0.3873, -0.10) m in the text).

issues.problem: Explanation gives omega = sqrt(3g/L) = 5.42 rad/s and then tip speed omega*L = 5.43 m/s for L = 1.0 m. These are the same number (sqrt(29.43) = 5.425), so the rounding is inconsistent. Key a (5.43) is still the only matching option.
issues.suggestedFix: Quote 5.42 or 5.43 consistently (5.425 m/s), or change option a to 5.42.

issues.problem: Worked example answer says 'alpha = 12.26 rad/s^2 (clockwise as drawn)' but no free-body diagram is provided, so the sense is undefined for the student.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'in the sense of the bar falling (clockwise if the free end is to the right of O)'.

issues.problem: Rolling-wheel top-point speed (2 v_G) is asked repeatedly in near-duplicate form: planar-rigid-body-kinematics.rotation-and-general-motion q002 and q006, and instantaneous-centre.locating-the-ic q002, with the same worked example in both lessons.
issues.suggestedFix: Vary one of the items (for example a point at an angle from the top, or a skidding wheel) to avoid repetition across units.
